memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen - the work of an embroiderer. It was twenty cubits long and, like the curtains of the courtyard, five cubits high, with four posts and four bronze bases. The hooks and bands of the posts were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver." - Exod 38:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The surrounding curtains were plain white linen. The entrance curtain was blue, purple and scarlet, embroidered by a craftsman.

The door was the most beautiful thing on that wall. Deliberately so. Anyone walking through the camp would see colour where the way in was.

God made the entrance attractive. He did not hide it or make it forbidding.

That should shape how we represent Him. Too often Christians present the faith as a list of restrictions — the wall rather than the door. But the way in is Christ Himself, and He is not a burden to be endured. Taste and see that the Lord is good (Ps 34:8).

Notice the height as well. The curtain was five cubits, the same as the surrounding wall. The door did not tower over people intimidatingly. It was on their level.

That is what happened in the incarnation. The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us (John 1:14) — literally, "tabernacled" among us. God came down to our height so we could come in.

When people look at your life, do they see a wall or a door?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your faith look attractive or merely restrictive to those around you?
2. Have you presented Christianity as rules rather than as a person?
3. What one thing could make you more approachable to someone exploring faith?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let my life show the beauty of the way in, not just the boundaries. Make me approachable for Your sake. Amen.
